aliases: On a group ring identity related to the Alon-Jaeger-Tarsi conjecture
records.display_name: For nonsingular matrices over F_p, the stated mod-p group-ring identity implies its integral counterpart.

frontier.basis: pinned OpenConjecture real_open_conjecture label

importance.rationale: Algebraic lifting of a mod-p group-ring identity whose truth would imply AJT for small primes; technically focused but important because it would settle a major conjecture.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
\label{41}
Let $p > 3$ be a prime and let $M$ be a nonsingular $n \times n$ matrix over $\mathbb{F}_p$ with
row vectors $a_1, \dots,a_n$, finally, let the standard basis vectors of $G:=\mathbb{F}_p^n$ be $e_1,\dots,e_n$.

\noindent
Then the $\mathbb{Z}$ group ring identity 
$$\prod_{1 \leq i \leq n} (1 - g^{e_i}) \cdot   \prod_{1 \leq i \leq n} (1 - g^{a_i})  = 0 \in \mathbb{Z}[G]$$
follows from the mod $p$ group ring identity 
$$\prod_{1 \leq i \leq n} (1 - g^{e_i}) \cdot   \prod_{1 \leq i \leq n} (1 - g^{a_i})  = 0 \in \mathbb{F}_p[G].$$
mathematical_statement.plain_text: Let $p > 3$ be a prime and let $M$ be a nonsingular $n x n$ matrix over $F_p$ with row vectors $a_1, ,a_n$, finally, let the standard basis vectors of $G:=F_p^n$ be $e_1,,e_n$. Then the $Z$ group ring identity $$_ 1 <= i <= n (1 - g^ e_i ) * _ 1 <= i <= n (1 - g^ a_i ) = 0 in Z[G]$$ follows from the mod $p$ group ring identity $$_ 1 <= i <= n (1 - g^ e_i ) * _ 1 <= i <= n (1 - g^ a_i ) = 0 in F_p[G].$$

model_label.evidence_snippet: Lines 126-135 and 140-146: "We proposed the following conjecture: ... Then the Z group ring identity ... follows from the mod p group ring identity ... When p large we proved it; small primes remain open."
model_label.interestingness_rationale: Algebraic lifting of a mod-p group-ring identity whose truth would imply AJT for small primes; technically focused but important because it would settle a major conjecture.

model_label.label_rationale: Conjecture 41 (lifting a mod p group-ring identity to Z[G]) is proposed by the authors and not proved here; they state it would imply AJT for remaining small primes.
model_label.viability_rationale: A concrete algebraic lifting statement; authors proved large-prime cases and the remaining small primes are a finite, targeted obstacle—amenable to focused algebraic or computational attack.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:

records.display_name: Every weighted graph excluding a fixed d-fat minor has a balanced separator coverable by O(sqrt(n)) bounded-radius balls.

frontier.basis: pinned OpenConjecture real_open_conjecture label

importance.rationale: Sharp coarse-separator statement generalizing the Robertson–Seymour sqrt(n) separator to fat minors; central in structural graph theory with significant structural and algorithmic consequences.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
\label{conj:fatminor-sep}
For every graph $H$ and $d\in \N$, there exist constants $c,r\in \N$ such that every $n$-vertex weighted graph $G$ that excludes $H$ as a~$d$-fat minor has a~$(c\sqrt{n},r)$-coverable balanced separator.

model_label.evidence_snippet: Abstract: we prove existence of separators coverable by c n^{1/2+ε} balls. Conjecture: there exist c,r such that every graph excluding H as a d-fat minor has a (c√n,r)-coverable balanced separator.
model_label.interestingness_rationale: Sharp coarse-separator statement generalizing the Robertson–Seymour sqrt(n) separator to fat minors; central in structural graph theory with significant structural and algorithmic consequences.
model_label.label: real_open_conjecture
model_label.label_rationale: The paper proves a coarse separator with c n^{1/2+ε} balls for every ε>0, and explicitly states the stronger c√n (no ε) version as a conjecture; it is not proved here.
model_label.viability_rationale: Authors already prove a cn^{1/2+ε} coverable separator and give an effective algorithm; the remaining ε appears a technical gap likely addressable but nontrivial, so plausible within five years.

aliases: Improved bound on symmetric differences of intersecting families
records.display_name: Every intersecting k-uniform family with n greater than 10k has at most the stated number of distinct symmetric differences.

frontier.basis: pinned OpenConjecture real_open_conjecture label

importance.rationale: A natural extremal-set problem analogous to classical intersecting-family results; resolving the n>10k range would close a clear gap and clarify structure of symmetric-difference extremals.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
Let $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\binom{[n]}{k}$ be an intersecting family with $n>10k$. Then
$$
|\mathcal{SD}(\mathcal{F})|\le\sum_{\ell=0}^{k-1}\binom{n-1}{2\ell}. 
$$

aliases: Van Vleck spectra of high-order Heun operators:\ finite-band universality and exterior asymptotics
records.display_name: The root-counting measures of high-order Heun spectral polynomials converge to a positive measure depending only on Q_k.

frontier.basis: pinned OpenConjecture real_open_conjecture label

importance.rationale: Links finite-band asymptotics, potential theory, and mother-body/critical-measure ideas; proving the tree-supported spectral limit would structurally characterize Van Vleck spectral limits for high-order Heun operators.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
\label{conj:mother-body}
Let $\dq$ be a high-order Heun operator with Fuchs index one and with generic
leading coefficient $Q_k$.  The root-counting measures of $Sp_n$ converge weakly
to a positive measure $\mu_{Q_k}$ depending only on $Q_k$.  Its support is a
finite planar tree
\[
        \Gamma_{Q_k}\subset K_Q,
\]
whose leaves are the roots of $Q_k$.  Moreover
\[
        U^{\mu_{Q_k}}(t)=U^{\nu_\dq}(t)
\]
in the exterior of $K_Q$; equivalently, $\mu_{Q_k}$ has the same exterior Cauchy
transform as the averaged finite-band measure $\nu_\dq$.  Thus $\mu_{Q_k}$ is a
positive mother body for the exterior field determined by the finite-band
averaging procedure.
mathematical_statement.plain_text: Let $$ be a high-order Heun operator with Fuchs index one and with generic leading coefficient $Q_k$. The root-counting measures of $Sp_n$ converge weakly to a positive measure $_ Q_k $ depending only on $Q_k$. Its support is a finite planar tree \[ _ Q_k subset K_Q, \] whose leaves are the roots of $Q_k$. Moreover \[ U^ _ Q_k (t)=U^ _ (t) \] in the exterior of $K_Q$; equivalently, $_ Q_k $ has the same exterior Cauchy transform as the averaged finite-band measure $_$. Thus $_ Q_k $ is a positive mother body for the exterior field determined by the finite-band averaging procedure.

model_label.evidence_snippet: Lines 1311–1316: 'We therefore propose the following refinement... \begin{conjecture}[Mother-body form of the spectral limit] ... The root-counting measures of Sp_n converge weakly to a positive measure...' and Problem asking to prove it (lines 1334–1336).
model_label.interestingness_rationale: Links finite-band asymptotics, potential theory, and mother-body/critical-measure ideas; proving the tree-supported spectral limit would structurally characterize Van Vleck spectral limits for high-order Heun operators.
model_label.label: real_open_conjecture
model_label.label_rationale: The paper explicitly poses this as a conjecture and a Problem asking to prove it; no proof or counterexample is provided here.
model_label.viability_rationale: Paper provides finite-band representation and a reduction to uniqueness; missing variational/S‑property characterization is concrete but nontrivial. Clear route exists, so moderate near-term solvability is plausible.

records.display_name: The shifted signed stable CSM Schur coefficient polynomials have nonnegative binomial-basis coefficients whose nonzero sequence is log-concave.

frontier.basis: pinned OpenConjecture real_open_conjecture label

importance.rationale: Extends shifted-binomial log-concavity to stable Chern--Schwartz--MacPherson Schur coefficients, tying positivity phenomena to equivariant characteristic classes with broad enumerative implications.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
Let $\lambda$ be a partition with parts at least $2$, and let
\[
c=\operatorname{codim}Y_\lambda=|\lambda|-\ell(\lambda).
\]
For every $f\ge c$, consider the homogeneous degree $f$ part of the stable
Chern--Schwartz--MacPherson class of the open coincident root stratum
$Y_\lambda(d)$:
\[
c^{SM}(Y_\lambda(d))_f.
\]
Expand it in the two-variable Schur basis as
\[
c^{SM}(Y_\lambda(d))_f
=
\sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor f/2\rfloor}
C_{\lambda,f,i}(d)\,s_{f-i,i}(a,b),
\]
where each $C_{\lambda,f,i}(d)$ is a polynomial in $d$ in the stable range.

Define the signed Schur coefficient polynomial
\[
\widetilde C_{\lambda,f,i}(d)
=
(-1)^{f-c}C_{\lambda,f,i}(d).
\]
Set
\[
y=d-|\lambda|-2(f-c).
\]
Then the shifted polynomial
\[
\widetilde C_{\lambda,f,i}\bigl(y+|\lambda|+2(f-c)\bigr)
\]
has a nonnegative expansion in the binomial basis:
\[
\widetilde C_{\lambda,f,i}\bigl(y+|\lambda|+2(f-c)\bigr)
=
\sum_{j\ge 0}
\gamma_{\lambda,f,i,j}\binom{y}{j},
\qquad
\gamma_{\lambda,f,i,j}\ge 0.
\]
Moreover, after deleting possible initial zeros, the coefficient sequence
\[
\left(\gamma_{\lambda,f,i,0},
\gamma_{\lambda,f,i,1},
\gamma_{\lambda,f,i,2},
\ldots
\right)
\]
is log-concave:
\[
\gamma_{\lambda,f,i,j}^{\,2}
\ge
\gamma_{\lambda,f,i,j-1}\gamma_{\lambda,f,i,j+1}
\qquad
\text{for all } j.
\]

records.display_name: For a general smooth member of every irreducible real equiclassical family, the associated class line bundle is nonspecial, equivalently the stated cohomology group vanishes and the focal map has maximal rank.

frontier.basis: pinned OpenConjecture real_open_conjecture label

importance.rationale: A cohomology vanishing controlling maximal rank of the focal map; deep deformation-theoretic content with clear geometric consequences for equiclassical/focal families in algebraic geometry.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
\label{conj:main}
Let $W$ be an irreducible component of the real equiclassical family of curves in $(\bP^2)^\vee$  of degree $c$, genus $g$, and class $d$, and let $G$ be a general smooth point of $W$, corresponding to a dual curve $D$ with normalization $\nu:\widetilde D\to D$. Let $\A$ be the class line bundle on $\widetilde D$ associated with $D$. Then $\A$ is nonspecial, i.e.,
\[
H^1(\A)=0.
\]
Equivalently, one has
\[
H^1(\mathcal I_{Z^{ec}}(c-1))=0,
\]
and hence the differential of the focal map has maximal rank $2c$ at $G$.

Let $$ be the class line bundle on $ D$ associated with $D$. records.display_name: As opposite labels coalesce in the stated topological Yang-Mills-Higgs problem, matter energy diverges under full back-reaction and curvature obeys the stated dimension-dependent four- and two-dimensional asymptotics.

frontier.basis: pinned OpenConjecture real_open_conjecture label

importance.rationale: Asserts detailed YMH back-reaction and curvature concentration behaviour (instanton scaling, dimension split). Significant within gauge-theory/geometric analysis and for the paper's interpretations, but focused in scope.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
\label{conj:proximity-curvature}
Let $M$ be a closed oriented Riemannian manifold with non-zero
relevant topological invariant, and let $D=\{(x_+,+1),(x_-,-1)\}$ be
two oppositely-labelled points at geodesic distance $d$. The YMH
minimiser $(A^*,\phi^*)$ satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2em]
\item \emph{(Matter-sector divergence, every dimension.)} The
matter-sector energy $\int_M\|D_{A^*}\phi^*\|^2$ diverges as
$d\to 0$, with the rate set by the regularised Green's kernel of
Paper~1 \cite[Theorem~13.3]{Vasii2026Paper1}. This is the dominant
contribution to the YMH energy in every dimension. (At leading order,
with $A^*$ fixed at the BPS connection in the moduli approximation,
this part is established by
Theorem~\ref{thm:proximity-scaling-curved}, with exponent
$\min(2\nu-n,2)$; the conjectural content is its persistence under
full back-reaction, $A^*=A^*(d)$.)
\item \emph{(Curvature behaviour, dimension-dependent.)}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),leftmargin=2em]
\item For $n=4$ ($SU(2)$ on a four-manifold, the $\sph{4}$ instanton
of this section), the curvature concentrates into a single core at
the midpoint geodesic of $(x_+,x_-)$ with scale $\lambda\sim d$,
peak $\|\Curv_{A^*}\|_{\max}\sim 1/d^2$; the Yang--Mills energy stays
fixed at $8\pi^2|c_2|$ by conformal invariance, with the topological
integral $\int_M\tr(\Curv_{A^*}\wedge\Curv_{A^*})=8\pi^2 c_2$
unchanged.
\item For $n=2$ ($U(1)$ on a surface, the $\sph{2}$ monopole of
\S\ref{sec:S2-monopole}), no scale family is available at
$\lambda=0$; the leading-order ($\phi=0$) gauge field is the unique
constant-curvature connection with
$\int_M\Curv_{A^*}=2\pi i\,c_1$, and the deformation by $J(\phi)$
as $d\to 0$ is bounded in amplitude. The Yang--Mills energy stays
at the uniform-monopole minimum $4\pi^2 c_1^2/\mathrm{Vol}(M)$ up to
$o(1)$ corrections; no $1/d^2$ peak appears.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

frontier.basis: pinned OpenConjecture real_open_conjecture label

importance.rationale: A naïve Iritani blowup formula tested in examples: a structural prediction in quantum cohomology/atom theory with clear consequences for blowups, significant within the subfield though not a broad flagship problem.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
\label{cIritani}
Let $\widetilde{X}$ be the blowup of $X$ in a smooth codimension $c$ subvariety $Z$. Suppose that the inclusion $Z \hookrightarrow X$ induces an embedding $\mathrm{N}_1 (Z, \mathbb{Z}) \hookrightarrow \mathrm{N}_1 (X, \mathbb{Z})$. Then the naive atomic decomposition of $\widetilde{X}$ is the sequence obtained by concatenating and sorting the naive atomic decompositions of $X$ and $(c-1)$ times the naive atomic decomposition of $Z$.

records.display_name: Every polynomial-dimensional circuit dynamical Lie algebra admits a representation in which the stated simulation preprocessing is polynomial-resource.

frontier.basis: pinned OpenConjecture real_open_conjecture label

importance.rationale: A practical organizing conjecture for Lie-algebraic simulation: if DLAs grow polynomially, efficient symmetry-adapted preprocessing likely exists. Valuable for quantum-classical simulation, with moderate theoretical depth.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
\label{conj:gsim_from_poly_dim}
Let $\mathfrak{g}\subseteq\mathfrak{u}(2^n)$ be a compact Lie algebra arising as the dynamical Lie algebra (or an invariant operator subspace for the adjoint action) of a family of circuits, with $\dim(\mathfrak{g})=\poly(n)$. mathematical_statement.body_tex:
\cite[Conjecture 2 (ii)]{ELX}\label{ELXc}
   Let $n\geq 3$ and $\U_n$ be a non-degenerate Hermitian variety in $\PP^n(\Fqt)$. If $V(F)$ is a hypersurface of degree $d\leq q$, then 
   $$M_n(d)=\max_{V(F)} |V(F)(\Fqt)\cap \U_n|=\begin{cases}
       d|\U_{n-1}(\Fqt)|-(d-1)|\U_{n-2}(\Fqt)| \ \text{if} \ n \ \text{is even}\\
       (dq^2-d+1)|\U_{n-2}(\Fqt)|+d\ \text{if} \ n \ \text{is odd},
   \end{cases}$$ 
   and this maximum is attained if and only if the hypersurface $V(F)$ is union of $d$ distinct hyperplanes $\Sigma_1, \Sigma_2,\dots, \Sigma_d$ such that each of the hyperplanes contains a common $(n-2)$-dimensional linear space $\Pi_{n-2}$  and $\Pi_{n-2}\cap \U_n$ is a non-degenerate Hermitian variety and: 

     --- If $n$ is even, the $d$ hyperplanes $\Sigma_1,\dots, \Sigma_d$ are non-tangent to $\U_n$.

     
     --- If $n$ is odd, the $d$ hyperplanes $\Sigma_1,\dots, \Sigma_d$ are tangent to $\U_n$.

   Let $n\geq 3$ and $\U_n$ be a non-degenerate Hermitian variety in $\PP^n(\Fqt)$. If $V(F)$ is a hypersurface of degree $d\leq q$, then 
   $$M_n(d)=\max_{V(F)} |V(F)(\Fqt)\cap \U_n|=\begin{cases}
       d|\U_{n-1}(\Fqt)|-(d-1)|\U_{n-2}(\Fqt)| \ \text{if} \ n \ \text{is even}\\
       (dq^2-d+1)|\U_{n-2}(\Fqt)|+d\ \text{if} \ n \ \text{is odd},
   \end{cases}$$ 
   and this maximum is attained if and only if the hypersurface $V(F)$ is union of $d$ distinct hyperplanes $\Sigma_1, \Sigma_2,\dots, \Sigma_d$ such that each of the hyperplanes contains a common $(n-2)$-dimensional linear space $\Pi_{n-2}$  and $\Pi_{n-2}\cap \U_n$ is a non-degenerate Hermitian variety and: 

     --- If $n$ is even, the $d$ hyperplanes $\Sigma_1,\dots, \Sigma_d$ are non-tangent to $\U_n$.

     
     --- If $n$ is odd, the $d$ hyperplanes $\Sigma_1,\dots, \Sigma_d$ are tangent to $\U_n$.

records.display_name: Infinitely many n satisfy the stated uniform upper bounds for both omega(n-k) and Omega(n-k) over the indicated ranges of k.

frontier.basis: pinned OpenConjecture real_open_conjecture label

importance.rationale: A sharper quantitative Erdős conjecture giving near‑optimal logarithmic bounds on distinct prime factors; technically deeper than linear bounds and relevant to extremal distribution questions in number theory.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
\label{conj:erdos679}
    For $\e>0$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that $$\omega(n-k) \le (1+\e) \frac{\log k}{\log \log k}$$ for all integers $1 \ll_\e  k <n$. 
    \begin{comment}
    Additionally, for infinitely many $n$ we have
    \[
    \omega(n-k) \le \frac{\log k}{\log \log k}+O \left( \frac{\log k}{(\log \log k)^2} \right)
    \]
    for all integers $1 \ll k<n$.
    \end{comment}
    Moreover, there are infinitely many $n$ such that
    \[
    \Omega(n-k) \le (1+\e) \frac{\log k}{\log 2}
    \]
    for all integers $1 \ll_\e k <n$.
mathematical_statement.plain_text: For $>0$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that $$(n-k) <= (1+) k k $$ for all integers $1 _ k <n$. comment Additionally, for infinitely many $n$ we have \[ (n-k) <= k k +O ( k ( k)^2 ) \] for all integers $1 k<n$. comment Moreover, there are infinitely many $n$ such that \[ (n-k) <= (1+) k 2 \] for all integers $1 _ k <n$.

model_label.interestingness_rationale: A sharper quantitative Erdős conjecture giving near‑optimal logarithmic bounds on distinct prime factors; technically deeper than linear bounds and relevant to extremal distribution questions in number theory.

aliases: Inhomogeneous Approximation by Sums of Roots
records.display_name: For every d at least 2 and k at least 1, suitable weighted shifted d-th roots admit cancellation through order dk-1, yielding g_{k,d}(N) of order at most N^{-(k-1/d)}.

frontier.basis: pinned OpenConjecture real_open_conjecture label

importance.rationale: Concrete Taylor-cancellation construction that would deliver the conjectural integer-target exponent; a strong, explicit mechanism in analytic number theory, but narrower than the uniform conjecture.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
\label{conj:taylor}
For every $d\geq 2$ and $k\geq 1$, there exist positive integers $A_i$, integers $u_i,v_i$, and a nonzero real constant $\lambda$ such that, for infinitely many integers $M$,
\[
  \sum_{i=1}^k A_i\left((M+u_i)^d+v_i\right)^{1/d}
  =L(M)+\lambda M^{-(dk-1)}+O_{d,k}(M^{-dk}),
\]
where $L(M)$ is an integer-valued linear polynomial in $M$.
Equivalently, after absorbing the weights $A_i$ into the radicands, one obtains
\[
  g_{k,d}(N)\ll_{d,k} N^{-(k-1/d)}
\]
for all sufficiently large $N$.

Equivalently, after absorbing the weights $A_i$ into the radicands, one obtains \[ g_ k,d (N)_ d,k N^ -(k-1/d) \] for all sufficiently large $N$.

importance.rationale: Asserts independence of a subdominant analytic-torsion term under isolated singular degenerations; significant within analytic/Arakelov degeneration theory but largely specialized to complex-analytic geometry.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
\label{conj:indep:rho}
If ${\rm Sing}\,X_{0}$ is isolated, $\xi={\mathcal O}_{X}$ and $n>1$, then $\varrho_{\pi, K_{X/S}(m)}$ is independent of the choice of 
an ample line bundle $H$ and $m>0$. Moreover, 
$$
\varrho_{\pi, K_{X/S}(m)}-\varrho_{\pi, K_{X/S}} = \dim \ker \square_{X_{0}}^{(0, n-1)} - h^{0,n-1}(X_{s}), 
\qquad
s\not=0.
$$ 
Here $\square_{X_{0}}^{(0,n-1)}$ is the Friedrichs extension of the Hodge-Kodaira Laplacian acting on the compactly supported 
smooth $(0,n-1)$-forms on $X_{0}\setminus{\rm Sing}\,X_{0}$.

\label{conj:spectral_sum_extremal_graphs}

\[
\lambda_1(G)+\lambda_2(G)\leq \lambda_1(K(n,p,q))+\lambda_2(K(n,p,q)),
\]
where if $n=7k+r$ with $0\leq r\le 6$, then 
\[
(p,q)= 
\begin{cases}
(2k,2k) & \text{if }r=0,1;\\
(2k+1,2k) & \text{if }r=2;\\
(2k+1,2k+1) & \text{if }r=3, 4;\\
(2k+2,2k+1) &\text{if }r=5;\\
(2k+2,2k+2) &\text{if }r=6.
\end{cases} 
\] 
Moreover, equality holds if and only if $G\cong K(n,p,q)$.

aliases: LAWS: Learning from Actual Workloads Symbolically -- A Self-Certifying Parametrized Cache Architecture for Neural Inference, Robotics, and Edge Deployment
records.display_name: No stationary online inference-caching algorithm has worst-case acquisition cost little-o of 2^H log N expert creations.

frontier.basis: pinned OpenConjecture real_open_conjecture label

importance.rationale: An information-theoretic lower bound matching the proposed upper bound would establish acquisition-optimality of LAWS; conceptually important within online caching theory though proof is technical.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
\label{conj:lower_rate}
No online inference caching algorithm can achieve acquisition cost
$o(2^{H(P_{\mathcal{M}})} \cdot \log N)$ expert creations in the worst case
over stationary distributions with entropy $H$.

\emph{Sketch.}
This is an information-theoretic lower bound: to achieve hit rate $H_\infty$
on a distribution with $2^H$ equally-probable heavy nodes, any algorithm must
``discover'' each heavy node at least once.  In the online setting (queries
arrive sequentially, no lookahead), the first discovery of node $n^*_k$ requires
at least one query that hits $n^*_k$.  The expected number of queries to first
hit all $2^H$ nodes is $\Omega(2^H \log 2^H) = \Omega(2^H \cdot H)$ by the
standard coupon collector lower bound.  Divided by the $N_{\min}$ threshold,
this gives $\Omega(2^H \cdot H / N_{\min})$ expert creations.  Since $H \leq \log_2 N$
(by the AEP), this matches the upper bound $O(2^H \log N)$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:growth}
to within constant factors, establishing that LAWS is \emph{acquisition-optimal}
among stationary online caching algorithms.  Formal proof requires a coupon-collector
lower bound argument in the online setting, which is standard but involves careful
handling of adaptive query distributions.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. If $ n\equiv10\pmod{24} $, then $n$ can be expressed as
\[
n = x^{2} + y^{2} + (2^{a}3^{b})^{2},
\]
where $x,y,a,b$ are non-negative integers and $b>0$. If $ n\equiv5\pmod{12} $, then $n$ can be expressed as
\[
n = x^{2} + y^{2} + (2^{a}5^{b})^{2},
\]
where $x,y,a,b$ are non-negative integers and $a>0$.

If $ n1024 $, then $n$ can be expressed as \[ n = x^ 2 + y^ 2 + (2^ a 3^ b )^ 2 , \] where $x,y,a,b$ are non-negative integers and $b>0$. If $ n512 $, then $n$ can be expressed as \[ n = x^ 2 + y^ 2 + (2^ a 5^ b )^ 2 , \] where $x,y,a,b$ are non-negative integers and $a>0$.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
\label{conj:macdonald-pivots} 
Let
$(\mu,\nu,\lambda)\sim_p(\tilde \mu,\tilde\nu,\tilde\lambda)$ be a one-box pivot $p\in \sigma \cap \tilde \sigma$ with common hook $h$.  Then we have the following congruence of shifted Macdonald Littlewood--Richardson coefficients,
\[
t^{-n(\sigma)} g_{\mu\nu}^{\lambda}(q,t)
\equiv
t^{-n(\tilde\sigma)}  g_{\tilde\mu\tilde\nu}^{\tilde\lambda}(q,t)
\pmod h.
\]

aliases: Helly Theorems for Generalized Turán Problems
records.display_name: The stated path extremal function obeys the proposed upper-bound versus Omega(n^(k+1)) dichotomy.

frontier.basis: pinned OpenConjecture real_open_conjecture label

importance.rationale: Sharp exponent prediction for paths in generalized Turán problems; tight in many cases and would refine Helly-type combinatorial tools, yet its significance is focused on extremal/path-specific questions.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
\label{optimal path conjecture}
		Let $k,t$ be integers with $k\ge 2$ and $t\ge 2k+1$.  If $0\le r\le k-2$ is the unique integer such that $t-3\equiv r \mod k-1$, then every family of graphs $\c{F}$ either satisfies
		\[\ex(n,P_t,\c{F})=O(\ex(n,\c{F})^{r+2}n^{k-2-r}),\]

aliases: On the Graphical $r$-Stirling Numbers of the First Kind for Specific Graph Families
records.display_name: The graphical Stirling-number sequence of every planar graph is unimodal.

frontier.basis: pinned OpenConjecture real_open_conjecture label

importance.rationale: Unimodality for all planar graphs is a natural, nontrivial enumerative-combinatorics conjecture over a large graph class; meaningful within combinatorics but not a cross-field flagship problem.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
\label{conj:unimodal-planar}
For any planar graph $G$ of order $n$, the sequence of graphical Stirling numbers
\[
\{\st{G}{k}\}_{k=1}^n
\]
is \emph{unimodal}, i.e., there exists an index $k_0$ such that
\[
\st{G}{1} \le \cdots \le \st{G}{k_0} \ge \cdots \ge \st{G}{n}.
\]
This property is known for paths, cycles, trees, lollipop, and Tadpole graphs.
mathematical_statement.plain_text: For any planar graph $G$ of order $n$, the sequence of graphical Stirling numbers \[ G k _ k=1 ^n \] is unimodal, i.e., there exists an index $k_0$ such that \[ G 1 <= <= G k_0 >= >= G n . \] This property is known for paths, cycles, trees, lollipop, and Tadpole graphs.

model_label.evidence_snippet: Lines 1789–1796: '\begin{conjecture} For any planar graph $G$ ... the sequence of graphical Stirling numbers \{${G\brack k}$\} is unimodal ... \end{conjecture}.'
model_label.interestingness_rationale: Unimodality for all planar graphs is a natural, nontrivial enumerative-combinatorics conjecture over a large graph class; meaningful within combinatorics but not a cross-field flagship problem.
model_label.label: real_open_conjecture
model_label.label_rationale: The unimodality for arbitrary planar graphs is posed as an open conjecture in the paper's 'Further Work and Open Problems' and is not proved here.
model_label.viability_rationale: Broad unimodality for all planar graphs is a wide generalization; known for special families but no clear finite reduction, so resolution within five years seems unlikely.

records.display_name: A tree is determined up to isomorphism by its Laplacian spectrum together with its (n-2,2) support-forest profile.

frontier.basis: pinned OpenConjecture real_open_conjecture label

importance.rationale: Posits that Laplacian plus (n-2,2)-spectral data uniquely determine trees—an appealing, nontrivial conjecture in spectral graph theory with clear structural consequences for tree invariants.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
Let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be trees on $n$ vertices.  If $T_1$ and $T_2$ have the
same Laplacian spectrum and the same $(n-2,2)$ support-forest profile, then
$T_1$ and $T_2$ are isomorphic.
Equivalently, no two non-isomorphic trees have identical $(n-1,1)$- and
$(n-2,2)$-spectra.

records.display_name: The stated rational system has solutions only at x=(r-1)^2/2, where the solution is unique up to scaling and permutation and is the regular root-of-unity configuration.

frontier.basis: pinned OpenConjecture real_open_conjecture label

importance.rationale: A concrete uniqueness/nonexistence statement for a symmetric rational equilibrium system arising in generalized Lamé and finite-gap theory—meaningful in integrable systems but relatively narrow in scope.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
\label{conj_Trei_rational}
The system 
\[
    \sum_{\nu\neq \mu}\Big( \frac{1}{(\alpha_\mu-\alpha_\nu)^3} + \frac{1}{(\alpha_\mu + \alpha_\nu)^3} \Big) + \frac{x}{\alpha_\mu^3}=0, \text{ for }\mu=1,\dots,r.
\]
has no solution for $x \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \{  \frac{1}{2}(r-1)^2 \}$. For $x = \frac{1}{2}(r-1)^2$, the solution is unique up to permutation and scaling and takes the form:
\[
    [\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r] = M [ 1, \zeta, \zeta^2, \dots, \zeta^{r-1} ]
\]
where $M \in \mathbb{C}^*$ and $\zeta = e^{\pi i / r}$ is a primitive $2r$-th root of unity.
mathematical_statement.plain_text: The system \[ _ != ( 1 (_-_)^3 + 1 (_ + _)^3 ) + x _^3 =0, for =1,,r. \] has no solution for $x in C 1 2 (r-1)^2 $. For $x = 1 2 (r-1)^2$, the solution is unique up to permutation and scaling and takes the form: \[ [_1,,_r] = M [ 1, , ^2, , ^ r-1 ] \] where $M in C^*$ and $ = e^ i / r $ is a primitive $2r$-th root of unity.

records.display_name: The stated restricted zero-sum sequences satisfy the MMS subset-count lower bound when n is at least (3+epsilon)k.

frontier.basis: pinned OpenConjecture real_open_conjecture label

importance.rationale: A restricted MMS variant near the 3k threshold under extra structural constraints; useful for specific reductions (e.g. to probabilistic conjectures) but more specialized.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
\label{q:MMS_variant}
For any constants $\eps, C>0$, and every sufficiently large integers $n, k$ satisfying $n\geq (3+\eps)k$, we have the following. Let $x_1, \dots, x_n$ be real numbers whose sum is $0$, such that at most $C$ among them are nonnegative and such that any two negative values $x_i, x_j$ are equal. Then, at least $\binom{n-1}{k-1}$ of the $k$-element subsets $S\subseteq [n]$ have nonnegative sum.

records.display_name: For a generic smooth real Weierstrass cubic, the compact oval is nonseparating and its exterior Cauchy transform is not algebraic.

frontier.basis: pinned OpenConjecture real_open_conjecture label

importance.rationale: A concrete elliptic-period cancellation test for smooth Weierstrass cubics; reduces non-algebraicity to explicit elliptic-function computations—useful as a positive-genus test but narrowly focused.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
\label{conj:smooth-cubic}
For a generic smooth real Weierstrass cubic in the above affine Euclidean model, the compact oval is nonseparating and the exterior Cauchy transform of the domain bounded by it is not algebraic. importance.rationale: A concrete degree formula for a class of quadratic-enriched rational maps has clear consequences for computing CC degrees and links geometry to quantum chemistry, but is a specialist algebro-geometric statement with limited cross-field reach.

mathematical_statement.body_tex:
Consider the rational map $\gamma: \mathbb P^m \dashrightarrow \mathbb P^{m+s}$ such that 
\[ \begin{matrix}
\gamma: & \mathbb P^m \setminus \textrm{V}(z_0) & \longrightarrow & \mathbb P^{m+s}\\
& z & \mapsto & y 
\end{matrix} \quad \text{with} \quad y_i = \begin{cases}
    z_0^2 & \text{if }i=0,\\
    z_0z_i & \text{if } i \in \{1,\ldots,m\},\\
    \gamma_i(z) & \text{if } i \in \{ m+1, \ldots, m+s\},
\end{cases}
\]
where $\gamma_i(z)$ are general homogeneous quadratic polynomials for $i=m+1,\ldots, m+s$. Then the graph of $\gamma$ has degree
\[ \deg(\text{graph}(\gamma)) = \begin{cases}
(m - s + 2)2^s -1 & \text{if } s<m, \\
2^{m+1}-1 & \text{if } s \geq m.
\end{cases} \]

Let $T$ be a general tensor of format $(a+1,b+1,n+2)$, where $n=a+b$, and $a,b\geq2$.

has codimension $\binom{a+b-1}{a}\binom{a+b-1}{b}-\binom{a+b-2}{a}\binom{a+b-2}{b}(a+b+2)$.
